# One complete PBF/1 exchange, byte by byte

*Generated by `tools/annotate.py` from the bytes that the real `pbf` client and `pbfd` server exchanged - do not edit by hand.
Regenerate with `make hexdump`; `make hexdump-check` fails if this file is out of date.*

Command: `pbf -v -H "X-Trace: demo" localhost:9000/hello.txt` against `pbfd <root> 9000`, where `hello.txt` holds the
28 bytes `Hello, packed binary world!\n` and was last modified at Unix time 1760000000.
The `-H` option adds a header that is **not** in the table, so this one exchange shows both header mechanisms:
numbered names (1 byte) and a length-prefixed literal.

## REQUEST - 72 bytes on the wire (12 header + 60 payload)

```
offset  bytes                                            meaning
0000    7f 50 42 46                                      Magic: 0x7F "PBF"
0004    01                                               Version = 1
0005    01                                               Type = 1 (REQUEST)
0006    00 01                                            Seq = 1
0008    00 00 00 3c                                      Length = 60 (payload bytes that follow)
000c    01                                               Method = 1 (GET)
000d    00 0a                                            PathLen = 10
000f    2f 68 65 6c 6c 6f 2e 74 78 74                    Path "/hello.txt"
0019    04                                               Header count = 4
001a    01                                               Field 1: Tag = 1 (numbered: "Host")
001b    00 0e                                            ValueLen = 14
001d    6c 6f 63 61 6c 68 6f 73 74 3a 39 30 30 30        Value "localhost:9000"
002b    02                                               Field 2: Tag = 2 (numbered: "User-Agent")
002c    00 05                                            ValueLen = 5
002e    70 62 66 2f 31                                   Value "pbf/1"
0033    03                                               Field 3: Tag = 3 (numbered: "Accept")
0034    00 03                                            ValueLen = 3
0036    2a 2f 2a                                         Value "*/*"
0039    00                                               Field 4: Tag = 0 (literal name follows)
003a    07                                               NameLen = 7
003b    58 2d 54 72 61 63 65                             Name "X-Trace" (spelled out)
0042    00 04                                            ValueLen = 4
0044    64 65 6d 6f                                      Value "demo"
```

The client spells **0** of its three standard header names: `Host`, `User-Agent` and `Accept` are tags 1, 2 and 3. Only
`X-Trace` is written out (tag 0, then NameLen 7 and its 7 letters).

## RESPONSE - 132 bytes on the wire (12 header + 120 payload)

```
offset  bytes                                            meaning
0000    7f 50 42 46                                      Magic: 0x7F "PBF"
0004    01                                               Version = 1
0005    02                                               Type = 2 (RESPONSE)
0006    00 01                                            Seq = 1
0008    00 00 00 78                                      Length = 120 (payload bytes that follow)
000c    00 c8                                            Status = 200
000e    07                                               Header count = 7
000f    04                                               Field 1: Tag = 4 (numbered: "Content-Type")
0010    00 19                                            ValueLen = 25
0012    74 65 78 74 2f 70 6c 61 69 6e 3b 20 63 68 61 72  Value "text/plain; charset=utf-8"
0022    73 65 74 3d 75 74 66 2d 38                       (continued)
002b    05                                               Field 2: Tag = 5 (numbered: "Content-Length")
002c    00 02                                            ValueLen = 2
002e    32 38                                            Value "28"
0030    06                                               Field 3: Tag = 6 (numbered: "Server")
0031    00 06                                            ValueLen = 6
0033    70 62 66 64 2f 31                                Value "pbfd/1"
0039    07                                               Field 4: Tag = 7 (numbered: "Last-Modified")
003a    00 0a                                            ValueLen = 10
003c    31 37 36 30 30 30 30 30 30 30                    Value "1760000000"
0046    08                                               Field 5: Tag = 8 (numbered: "ETag")
0047    00 0d                                            ValueLen = 13
0049    22 31 63 2d 36 38 65 37 37 38 30 30 22           Value ""1c-68e77800""
0056    09                                               Field 6: Tag = 9 (numbered: "Cache-Control")
0057    00 08                                            ValueLen = 8
0059    6e 6f 2d 63 61 63 68 65                          Value "no-cache"
0061    0a                                               Field 7: Tag = 10 (numbered: "Accept-Ranges")
0062    00 04                                            ValueLen = 4
0064    6e 6f 6e 65                                      Value "none"
0068    48 65 6c 6c 6f 2c 20 70 61 63 6b 65 64 20 62 69  Body: all 28 remaining payload bytes = "Hello, packed binary world!\n"
0078    6e 61 72 79 20 77 6f 72 6c 64 21 0a              (continued)
```

Seq is `1`, copied from the request. There is no body length anywhere: the body is whatever is left of the payload after
the last header, i.e. `Length - 2 (Status) - (header list)` = 28 bytes. `Content-Length: 28` is only a hint.
`Last-Modified` is `1760000000` and the `ETag` is `"1c-68e77800"` (size and mtime in hex).

## Size

| | with numbered names | if every name were spelled out | saved |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| REQUEST payload | 60 | 80 | 20 |
| RESPONSE payload | 120 | 195 | 75 |

(A spelled-out field needs a 1-byte NameLen plus the name instead of a 1-byte Tag, so a table hit saves exactly the name's length.)
